issues.detail: Assertion 2 is complete:true and includes {"not_ran_git": ["checkout","restore","stash","reset","clean"]}. A correct Auditor gathering version-control evidence about cancelled-cycle residue could run read-only `git stash list` or `git stash show` to see whether other drafts exist, or `git clean -n` as a dry run. Either would fail the assertion even though nothing was reverted. Separately, the README `unchanged` check, head_unchanged, and the `not_ran_git: mutating` invariant already catch any real revert.
issues.fix: In auditor-13/spec.json, checks[2].all, change the not_ran_git list to ["checkout", "restore", "reset"] by removing "stash" and "clean". Alternatively, drop that check entirely and rely on `unchanged: [README.md]` plus the mutating invariant.

issues.detail: All commits share the timestamp 2026-10-04T12:30:00Z, including the commits recording the 2026-09-29 cancelled cycle. This is harmless; nothing in the case depends on commit dates.

summary: The fixture faithfully realizes the case. It is a valid DOCUMENTATION cycle in AUDITING whose BaselineReconciliation carries the cancelled documentation cycle's exact request. That cycle's uncommitted README draft is unstaged and mixes accurate claims with three the source contradicts, and check.mjs and all selfChecks pass. One check could fail a correct run: assertion 2's not_ran_git list includes "stash" and "clean", so a read-only `git stash list` or `git clean -n` would fail a complete:true assertion; removing those two entries fixes it.
